messages:
alice-cs: heads-up — Larkspur reported a sudden p99/tail latency increase for chat completions starting ~08:10 UTC. Customer reports timeouts and retries. escalated to us.

maria-sre: checking dashboards now, looking at tenant id lk-894. seeing p95 fine but p99 shoots up on inference-service-3 (us-west-2-dedicated pool).

devon-eng: can you paste the trace ids? I want to see if it's GPU queueing or k/v cache stalls.

alice-cs: customer gave example call ids: 0a1b2c3d, 0a1b2c4f, 0a1b2c9a. they say it started after a spike in their embed batch jobs earlier this morning.

maria-sre: pulling traces: 0a1b2c3d -> long scheduling delay ~450ms in request-queue, then 120ms inference. 0a1b2c4f similar. queue depth correlates with host: gpux-07 (same pool).

ops_oncall: quick check: gpux-07 shows CPU at 95% and GVM memory pressure. There are several tenants on that node; one tenant (unknown atm) has large embed jobs around 08:05. suspect noisy neighbor.

kenji-support: I reached out to Larkspur contact (copied) to confirm they kicked off a bulk embed run at 08:03. larkspur-contact: can you confirm?

larkspur-contact: yes, we ran a bulk embeddings job for updated product docs at 08:02 for ~12k texts, used /embeddings batch endpoint. we thought it would respect our reserved capacity.

maria-sre: interesting — reservation was for 8 rps but the batch size and concurrent clients pushed token throughput much higher. routing placed some work on dedicated pool gpux-07 where Larkspur shares with other tenants. queueing climbed.

devon-eng: do we have per-tenant scheduling isolation on that pool? I thought reservations should have isolated queues.

maria-sre: we have soft isolation at request routing, but the pool is mixed. reservations are capacity guarantees, but large short spikes can still cause transient queueing unless pinned.

alice-cs: customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they need the spikes to stop within the hour. what options?

devon-eng: short-term: move Larkspur traffic to a different host or a fallback model with lower memory footprint so their embeddings run faster per token and reduce queue time. Also can apply a temporary per-tenant burst throttle for other tenants on gpux-07.

ops_oncall: I can evict non-reserved workers off gpux-07 and re-route their traffic to gpux-09. that should free scheduling space. doing now — will report when routing changes propagate.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Routing change to balance-gpux-07 initiated by ops_oncall at 08:24 UTC.

maria-sre: also enabling a tenant-specific allowlist for Larkspur to pin their job to reserved workers would help permanently. but that requires tenant reservation config update and possible billing change (dedicated pin).

kenji-support: explained options to customer: 1) immediate: we can reroute their embed job to standby pool (may change latency slightly), 2) short-term: we can throttle heavy concurrent batch jobs across the pool, 3) long-term: offer pinning (allowlist) or increase reservation. they chose immediate reroute + follow-up on pinning.

ops_oncall: reroute completed at 08:28 UTC. gpux-07 queue depth dropped to baseline, Larkspur's calls now hitting gpux-11 (standby-dedicated).

alice-cs: customer confirms error rate went down and tail latencies improved but they still saw a couple of 5xx earlier. they're happy for now but want root cause and prevention plan.

maria-sre: root cause summary: uncoordinated high-throughput embed batch from Larkspur plus mixed tenancy on gpux-07 caused request queueing. the scheduler allowed tasks to be placed on gpux-07 where scheduling latency spiked.

devon-eng: follow-ups I'm adding: 1) improve scheduler heuristics to prefer pinned/reserved workers for reservation-bearing tenants, 2) add a short-circuit for very large batch jobs to check reservation quota before scheduling, 3) improve realtime admission control to cap transient token throughput per-node.

maria-sre: immediate mitigation steps completed: reroute customer -> gpux-11, evict non-reserved, enable temporary per-node throttle for embed-heavy clients. I'll open a runtime ticket for the scheduler changes.

kenji-support: I'll draft an email to Larkspur with timeline, what we changed, and options (pinning, increase reservation, schedule their bulk jobs off-peak).

larkspur-contact: thanks. can you also provide logs or a short play-by-play we can show our infra team? we have compliance audit next week.

alice-cs: yes — we'll send a postmortem-style timeline and include the traces and mitigation steps. keeping it short and actionable.

devon-eng: saved traces and logs: trace bundle link: https://internal.redwood/traces/lk-894/1799998888-bundle (internal-only). also adding a small repro: run 12 concurrent /embeddings calls with batch size 1k against our staging pool to emulate.

maria-sre: tagging for follow-up: runtime-ticket-4251 (scheduler heuristics), infra-ticket-6312 (per-node admission control), and cs-action-210 (customer comms + pinning offer).

ops_oncall: monitoring alert thresholds adjusted for gpux-07 to detect queueing spikes earlier. added an automated temporary eviction policy if queueing > 300ms for > 60s.

kenji-support: sending email to customer now, copying eng and SRE. will include suggested mitigation (pinning) and estimate for config change lead time (~2 business days).

alice-cs: nice work everyone. I'll close this channel once customer confirms postmortem receipt. thumbs up :thumbsup:

larkspur-contact: got the email. appreciate the quick response. we'll schedule bulk jobs for off-peak windows and discuss pinning.

maria-sre: marking thread for postmortem write-up. last note: consider adding a guidance doc to CS about how to recommend embedders to customers (batch sizing, concurrency, reserved capacity implications).

alice-cs: agreed — cs playbook item created: cs-playbook#embed-bulk-guidance.

sre-bot: incident-bot: Incident larkspur-latency-1799998888 recorded, severity: SEV3, owner: maria-sre.

alice-cs: closing thread — last update 08:44 UTC.
